drawdown_context: SLP FY24 10-K (fiscal year ended Aug 31, 2024, filed 2024-10-30) reported revenue of $70.0M (+18% YoY) and the closing of the $100.2M cash Pro-ficiency acquisition (June 2024) that added two new business units (ALI software, MC services). Headline software-licensed model continued, but FY24 overall gross margin collapsed from 80% to 62% (cost of revenue +131% YoY). Two pre-cutoff 10-Qs (Q1 FY25 filed 2025-01-08; Q2 FY25 filed 2025-04-04) and a pre-cutoff auditor-change 8-K (2025-04-18) supply the dispositive disclosure deltas. Forward return -50.1% from 2025-05-15 to 2026-05-15.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Item 9 ('Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure'): 'None.' Auditor disclosed as Rose, Snyder & Jacobs LLP (PCAOB Firm ID 468), a small Encino CA regional firm — same auditor that signed the FY24 10-K including the goodwill/intangibles arising from the freshly-closed $100M Pro-ficiency acquisition.
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_tracker.query_auditor_changes(cik='0001023459', cutoff_date='2025-05-15') for 8-K Item 4.01 disclosures in the lookback window; Mode B: did the auditor relationship survive the first full audit after the largest acquisition in Company history?
rfm_tuples.M_value: n_8k_item_401=1. 8-K filed 2025-04-18 (accession 0001628280-25-018292) discloses: 'The Audit Committee approved the dismissal of Rose, Snyder & Jacobs LLC ('RSJ') as the Company's independent registered public accounting firm and dismissed RSJ on April 15, 2025.' Replacement: Grant Thornton LLP (mid-tier, upgrade). 8-K asserts no disagreements and no reportable events. signal=UPGRADE_OR_LATERAL.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor was dismissed exactly one month before our cutoff, the first fiscal year-end after the Pro-ficiency acquisition. The change was characterized as a 'competitive process' with no disclosed disagreement, and the new firm (Grant Thornton) is an upgrade in size. However, the timing (immediately post the FY24 audit that signed off on $76.9M of new goodwill) and the fact that this is the FIRST audit committee 'competitive process' in the company's recent history (no prior 4.01 in 5-year lookback) is a yellow flag. Mode B finding.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K MD&A: 'Overall gross margin percentage was 62% and 80% for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2024, and 2023, respectively' — an 18-percentage-point compression in a single year. Driven by 'Cost of revenues increased by $15.2 million, or 131%... $6.8 million... due to the reorganization of our internal structure... $3.0 million... due to the acquisition of Pro-ficiency. $1.6 million... full year's recognition of expenses associated with the acquisition of Immunetrics.' Management frames the bulk as a reclassification (G&A → COGS) plus M&A integration cost, NOT structural.
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution + self_text on Q1/Q2 FY25 10-Qs: did gross margin recover toward 80% in FY25 as the 'reclassification' narrative implied (one-time noise) or did it stay compressed (structural)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY25 (3mo end Nov 30 2024, filed 2025-01-08): overall GM 54%, software 75%, SERVICES 26% (vs 47% prior year same quarter). Q2 FY25 (3mo end Feb 28 2025, filed 2025-04-04): overall GM 59%, software 81%, SERVICES 25% (vs 44% prior year). H1 FY25: services GM 25% vs 46% H1 FY24. Software GM also declined ~6pp YoY. Services revenue +26% YoY, services gross profit -30% YoY ($4.4M vs $6.2M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's 'reclassification + one-time M&A' framing for FY24 margin compression is falsified by Q1 and Q2 FY25 results — services gross margin has stabilized at ~25%, half of historical levels. The Pro-ficiency Medical Communications consulting business and the Immunetrics services book are STRUCTURALLY lower-margin than legacy SLP services. Services revenue is growing 26% but services gross profit is shrinking 30%. Pure mix-shift toward unit-economically inferior consulting revenue is being labeled as 'growth.'

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors: 'The Pro-ficiency business, which we acquired Company in June 2024, may not perform as we or the market expects.' Balance sheet at Aug 31 2024 shows $96.1M goodwill, of which $77.0M (~80%) is from Pro-ficiency (ALI $31.1M + MC $45.9M), against a Pro-ficiency purchase price of $100.2M. Implied PP&E and identifiable intangibles were only ~$23M of the $100M deal — i.e. 77% of purchase price went to goodwill on a six-month-old asset.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on Q1/Q2 FY25 10-Qs goodwill rollforward — were any triggering-event reviews disclosed, given services GM collapsed to 25% in both quarters? Mode B: 'goodwill at Pro-ficiency reporting units / Pro-ficiency revenue contribution' coverage ratio.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY25 10-Q goodwill rollforward (Note): Balance Aug 31 2024 = $96.078M (CPP $7.3M, QSP $11.8M, ALI $31.1M, MC $45.9M). Balance Feb 28 2025 = $96.305M — change is only a $0.227M measurement-period adjustment for Pro-ficiency net working capital settlement. ZERO impairment charges recognized. No 'triggering event' analysis disclosed despite ALI/MC GM running at ~25% vs underwriting assumptions, services gross profit shrinking YoY, and stock at $28 vs >$45 at deal announcement. Combined Pro-ficiency goodwill ($77.0M) is ~41% of total shareholders' equity ($189.5M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding. The 10-K disclosed Pro-ficiency execution risk in the abstract but did not flag goodwill concentration or impairment exposure. By Q2 FY25, ALI and MC are the two business units with the worst gross margins, services GP is contracting in dollars, and no impairment review is disclosed. Auditor change on April 15 2025 — Grant Thornton's first audit (FY25 year-end Aug 31 2025) will reasonably require a fresh goodwill review at fair value. The $77M Pro-ficiency goodwill is the largest disclosure-quality hazard on the balance sheet.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Note: Immunetrics earnout — 'The earnout target for the first measurement period was $4.0 million, however, based on revenue attainment, we only paid $2.5 million in March 2024... there is a catch-up opportunity for the second measurement period's earnout payment to increase from the target of $4.0 million to $5.5 million.' Framed as a still-open opportunity.
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution on 'Immunetrics' + 'earnout' in Q1/Q2 FY25 10-Qs to see whether the second earnout was paid as targeted.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY25 10-Q (Apr 4 2025): 'based on earned revenue for Immunetrics during the second earnout measurement period, the Company has assessed the fair value of the earnout liability to be zero. However, the final settlement with the sellers is pending, and while the Company does not anticipate any earnout payment, it is still subject to final determination.' Trajectory: $4.0M target → $2.5M actual (1st period) → $0 expected (2nd period). Total earnout: $2.5M against $9.5M total potential = 26% attainment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Immunetrics (acquired June 2023 for $7M cash + earnout) has materially underperformed. The 10-K's 'catch-up opportunity' framing is contradicted by the Q2 FY25 disclosure of zero expected payment. This is a direct, in-house track record signal that SLP's M&A revenue-modeling overstates target attainment — directly relevant to the freshly closed and 10x larger Pro-ficiency deal, where the same management team underwrote the $100M valuation and $77M goodwill.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K and Q2 FY25 press release (8-K filed 2025-04-03): SLP maintains 'fiscal 2025 revenue $90M-$93M' and 'adjusted diluted EPS $1.07-$1.20' full-year guidance, with H1 FY25 revenue of $41.4M (+26% YoY). rfm_tuples.M_value: RPO trajectory: Aug 31 2024 = $10.8M (97% in <12mo); Nov 30 2024 = $11.2M (97% in <12mo); Feb 28 2025 = $15.1M (98% in <12mo). H2 FY25 revenue required to hit low end of guidance: $90M - $41.4M = $48.6M. RPO at Feb 28 2025 covers only $15.1M of that, i.e. ~31% of H2 guidance is contracted; H1 already delivered $41.4M including $4.5M Q2 over-time recognition. The press release additionally disclosed 'backlog' of $20.4M (a non-GAAP metric distinct from RPO — backlog typically includes signed but not contractually-binding work). Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed from 39% (Q2 FY24) to 29% (Q2 FY25).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding. Maintaining 28-33% revenue growth and 31-33% adj EBITDA margin guidance with only ~31% of the required H2 revenue contracted (RPO) is aggressive given that H1 services GM ran at 25% and adj EBITDA already contracted 10 percentage points YoY. The 'backlog $20.4M' framing in the press release attempts to substitute a softer non-GAAP measure for the harder RPO. The guidance has high reversal risk into H2.

The Q1 FY25 cash flow statement (filed Jan 8 2025) is the first place this is visible to investors, and Q2 confirms the suspension. For a company that maintained a quarterly dividend through FY24 explicitly to signal stability, this is a non-trivial capital-action reversal that the 10-K did not explain. Mode B: combined with $21M of remaining cash post the $100M Pro-ficiency cash deal, the dividend suspension is consistent with management privately recognizing balance-sheet stress.

summary: SLP's FY24 10-K (filed Oct 2024) and the two pre-cutoff 10-Qs (Jan 8 and Apr 4 2025) plus an Apr 18 2025 auditor-change 8-K tell a coherent disclosure-quality short setup. Five hard pre-cutoff signals: (1) services gross margin permanently halved from 46% to 25% post-Pro-ficiency, with the 10-K's 'reclassification + transitional' framing falsified by both FY25 quarters; (2) $77M of $96M goodwill sits in Pro-ficiency ALI/MC units with no impairment review despite chronic services GM collapse; (3) the Immunetrics earnout track record (26% of total) is direct in-house evidence that SLP overpays for and over-models acquisitions, with the Pro-ficiency deal 10x larger; (4) the quarterly dividend was silently suspended in FY25 with no 10-K acknowledgment, against $21M residual cash; (5) the auditor (Rose Snyder & Jacobs) was dismissed exactly 30 days pre-cutoff immediately after signing the first post-acquisition audit, and replaced with Grant Thornton — a Mode B yellow flag whose first audit will inevitably stress-test the Pro-ficiency goodwill. Reaffirmed $90-93M guidance is backed by only ~31% RPO coverage of H2. Composite reflects multiple SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY signals concentrated on margin and goodwill — this is the kind of name the framework should flag, and the -50% forward return is consistent.
